key_insight: RheOFormer’s viscoplastic-flow prediction improves with logarithmic velocity representations, gradient-aware losses, and a few training cases covering missing physical regimes.
engineering_relevance: These remedies support more reliable, data-efficient CFD surrogates for flows containing both yielded regions and low-gradient, unyielded plugs.
method: Evaluate RheOFormer on steady Bingham channel flow across dataset structures, value ranges, and input representations.
Use logarithmic velocity representations and gradient-aware losses to improve plug-region predictions.
Add strategically selected training cases to reduce extrapolation errors.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports improved accuracy in challenging regimes and accurate steady-state prediction from one partially developed snapshot, outperforming simply copying the input.
watch_item: Evidence is limited to a simple channel geometry and Bingham constitutive model; generalization to more complex flows remains unestablished.
paper_title: Failure Modes and Data-Efficient Remedies for Transformer-Based Prediction of Viscoplastic Flows
